quay: Half a mile of granite, worn smooth by four hundred years of barrels. Everything Albra sells goes out across these stones, and everything it buys comes in. The gulls know the difference between a full sack and an empty one.
pier: Tarred planks on oak piles, numbered in brass. The houses rent them by the tide. A chalk board at the root says whose ship is in and whose is overdue.
crane: A treadwheel crane: two men walk inside the wheel and a ton of copper rises out of a hold. They are paid by the lift, and they sing.
customs: Where the city weighs, counts and taxes everything that crosses the quay, and where the four houses send their cleverest clerks to argue about it. Over the door: "THE SEA IS FREE. THE QUAY IS NOT."
harbourLight: The lighthouse on the mole. Its lamp burns whale oil, never a spell: the Varg reavers took it for a signal, once, and the houses have paid them a sea-toll every year since so that it never happens again.
fishmarket: Herring, cod, eels by the bucket and a crab the size of a shield that nobody will buy. The fishwives' prices are not negotiable and neither are their opinions.
ropewalk: The docks' long street, where rope was once twisted along its whole length. Now it is chandlers, sailmakers, net-menders, dockers' lodgings and taverns, and the rope is made in a shed at the end.
cargo: Crates stencilled with house marks: an anchor (Varenne), a flame over a hammer (Ashcombe), a winged scale (Quarrender). Somebody has chalked a fourth mark, a gold coin, on one of them, and somebody else has scrubbed most of it off.
quint: Iron-bound, sealed in three places, guarded by a man who will not meet your eye. Quintessence, going south to the Brazen Dominion, where they pay for it in silver and spend it on their war.
nets: Drying in the wind. The net-menders sit among them all day with bone needles, and they hear everything said on the quay.
shipyard: The last shipyard in Gilden that isn't owned by a house: a hull on the slip, half planked, and old Fettle shouting at it. Varenne wants the yard. Fettle wants Varenne in the harbour with a stone tied to him.
boats: Lighters and jolly-boats for taking cargo out to the ships too big for the piers. Each house paints its own a different colour, so a boat on the wrong side of the harbour is an argument.
seaGod: The Old Man of the Narrows
A sea-god nobody prays to any more, except the dockers, and the fishwives, and the captains, and the houses before a big cargo goes out. Coins in the basin at his feet.
saltpurse: The dockers' tavern on the Ropewalk, low-beamed and loud, with beds upstairs for sailors between ships and wizards between jobs. The landlady keeps a cudgel under the bar with each house's mark carved on it, so nobody can say she favours one.
shipping: House Varenne's shipping office, where passage is sold to the Mainland and beyond. A slate by the door lists the sailings: Halemouth (Hallowmark: no magic aboard), Brassmouth (the Dominion), Varrow, "and further, for a price".
exchange: A temple to money, and nobody pretends otherwise: the dome is gilt, the floor is marble, and at noon the four houses send their factors to shout prices at each other under it. Three of the four statues in its niches are of living people. The fourth niche is empty.
exchangeSq: The busiest square on Albra: money-changers, notaries, letter-writers, porters with handcarts and pickpockets with handcarts. A clock on a post tells the time to the minute, which is the only honest thing in the square.
guildhall: Where Gilden's guilds meet: carters, coopers, chandlers, lightermen, and the newest, the Guild of Hired Wizards, which the houses pretend not to have noticed. Its noticeboard is mostly fines.
counting: Narrow fronts, deep cellars, iron shutters. Every house on the row belongs to one of the four houses, or to someone who owes them money, which is the same thing.
well: The water is good. The bucket costs a copper. The copper goes to House Ashcombe, who dug it.
lamp: Lit at dusk by the city watch, who are paid by all four houses and trusted by none of them.
hill: The street of palaces. Each house has its gate, its gardens and its bravos on the gate; a stranger walking from one end to the other is watched by four different people, and noted in four different ledgers.
ashcombe: The seat of House Ashcombe: copper, tin and quintessence, down the Ore Road from the Anvilfells. A flame over a hammer on every banner. Its bravos wear red, and its carters swear by it.
varenne: The seat of House Varenne, who own the fleet: half the ships in the harbour fly the silver anchor. It is House Varenne that pays the Varg their sea-toll every spring, and House Varenne that never lets anyone forget it.
quarrender: The seat of House Quarrender, the newest of the great houses: bankers, and agents to the gnomes of Gimbaldry, whose airships moor on Beacon Hill. A winged scale on the banners. Their money is younger than the others', and they are the only house that doesn't mind saying so.
vellacourt: A palace with its banners taken down. The gate is chained, the garden gone to seed, and the gilt on the shutters has been scraped off by somebody with a knife. A gold coin is carved over the door; someone has tried to chisel it out and given up.
garden: Clipped hedges, gravel walks, a fountain with a house mark in the basin. A gardener rakes the gravel smooth behind you as you go.
bravo: Silk, in the house's colours. In Gilden you can tell who a man works for by the colour of his sash, and who he used to work for by the colour of the bruise.
oregate: Where the Ore Road comes in from Chepstead and Hollowmere, and the Anvilfells beyond. Copper and tin come in, salt, silver and cloth go out, and quintessence comes in sealed, under guard, and never stops moving.
yard: The great yard inside the Ore Gate, where caravans load and unload: wagons, oxen, mules, carters, and the houses' guards counting everything twice. It smells of tar, dung and money.
charters: Every caravan leaving Gilden posts a charter here: the house, the road, the cargo, the pay. Below them all in red: "BANDITS ON THE ORE ROAD. ESCORTS WANTED. WIZARDS PREFERRED, PAID DOUBLE." Below that, smaller, in another hand: "Ask who hired the bandits."
charterhouse: Where escorts are hired, paid and, now and then, buried. The Master of the Charterhouse keeps a ledger of every wizard who has ridden for every house, and the houses pay him well to read it.
wagons: Iron-tyred, tarred canvas, a house mark painted on the tailboard. The axle has been greased with something that smells of the Anvilfells.
ore: Copper ore from Copperhythe, green-streaked and heavy. The dwarves won't sell it smelted; they say it's better smelted, and they're right.
skyport: Beacon Hill, levelled and paved by the gnomes of Gimbaldry, who will moor nowhere else on Albra. When an airship is due, the whole hill is cleared, the mast lit, and the porters wait with their faces turned up like flowers.
mast: A tower of iron lattice and brass, with a ring at the top for an airship's nose. The gnomes built it in a week and charge the city rent for it.
skyOffice: House Quarrender sells passage on the gnome airships here. The prices on the board are in gold, and they are not a misprint.
kites: The gnomes fly them from the mast to read the wind before a ship comes in. Children chase their shadows across the paving.
shipSide: An Ashcombe merchantman riding at anchor, low in the water with Anvilfells copper for the Mainland. The crew are ashore; the purser is not, and is counting the cargo for the third time.
shipFront: Varenne's packet to Halemouth, moored bow out so she can slip the moment the tide turns. Every passenger is searched for charms before boarding: Hallowmark's witch-finders wait at the other end, and Varenne would rather lose a fare than a ship.
shipBack: Back from Ulfvik with furs, whale oil and a Varg pilot who sleeps on deck and will not come ashore. Her stern lanterns are lit day and night: a promise, the sailors say, to whoever is watching from the sea.
shipBow: Flying the Varenne pennant, but her crew speak with the Dominion's flat vowels and her hold was loaded under guard. Whatever she carries south, the Customs House was paid well not to weigh it.
shipStern: A fine ship with her name freshly painted over. The harbour boys say she was a Vellacourt ship once, and that the house mark still shows under the gilt when the light is low.
galleon: House Varenne's flagship, moored at the deep-water stage where nothing else in the harbour is allowed to tie up. Gilt on the stern, cannon behind the gunports, and a captain who has never once paid the Varg's sea-toll out of his own pocket.
airship: Moored nose-in to the gnomes' mast: a gasbag of patched silk under brass hoops, a gondola of riveted copper, a propeller as tall as a man. It hums. The gnomes say that is the engine. The porters say that is the gnomes.
stallCloth: Bolts of Mainland wool, Southland silk and dyed linen from the Ropewalk's vats, and a tapestry with a gold star on it that the clothier swears was woven for a queen. Which queen, he can't say.
stallBakery: Mutton pies, eel pies, apple pies and a loaf the length of your arm. The baker counts the Exchange clock by her ovens: when the noon shouting starts, the pies go up a penny.
stallCharms: Bottled cures, a skull of doubtful origin, a little brass orrery and a crystal 'charged under three moons'. None of it is magic. The stallholder knows that, and knows the sailors don't, and charges accordingly.
stallLamps: Rope by the coil and the fathom, lanterns, wicks and a spool of tarred twine. Every ship that leaves Gilden buys something here; every ship that comes back buys more.
stallTools: Hammers, tongs, crowbars and a box of nails sold by weight. Carters mend their wagons here before the Ore Road, and the tinker mends whatever they bring back.
coast: West along the shore to Ferryhythe, where Hallowmark's witch-finders search everyone off the ferry. The milestone says FERRYHYTHE 40; someone has scratched under it, WIZARDS 0.
